hub.sub: Retainer, project, hour block, dedicated team and hybrid models, what drives the cost of white-label SEO and PPC, and how to work out your margin.

answer.label: In short
answer.lead: White-label work is priced by a written scope under one of five models: a monthly retainer, a fixed project fee, a block of hours, a dedicated team or a hybrid. MMC invoices your agency in Indian rupees or US dollars, with a three-month minimum, and you set your client's price. We do not publish prices, because scope drives cost.
answer.hl: priced by a written scope under one of five models
answer.who: Monday Marketing Company (MMC) agrees a pricing model with each partner agency and works behind your brand. You own the client relationship; we do the work.

paras: No model is best. The right one depends on how predictable your demand is and how much flexibility you need. We do not publish prices, because the same service can mean very different work. The sections below explain what drives the cost, so you can judge any quote, ours included.

paras: Site size and technical state. A large site, or one with indexing, speed or structure problems, needs more audit and fix time.
Competition. A crowded market needs more content and more authority work to move.
Content volume. The number of pages, briefs and articles in scope each month.
Locations. Local SEO effort grows with each Google Business Profile, citation set and location page.
Link building. Editorial outreach is slow, skilled work and is priced as its own line.
Reporting. A short monthly summary costs less to produce than a detailed report with commentary for each client.
Accounts and campaigns. More accounts, campaigns and markets mean more daily management.
Platforms. Google Ads alone is less work than Google Ads with Meta or LinkedIn alongside.
Account condition. Broken tracking, a messy product feed or an account that needs rebuilding adds set-up work before optimisation starts.
Creative. Ad copy is part of management; new images, video or UGC are scoped separately.
Reporting cadence. Weekly reporting takes more time than monthly.
Ad spend is never part of the fee. The client pays the platform directly.

blocks.h: What drives the cost of a dedicated team
paras: Roles. You can add an SEO specialist, a PPC or paid social specialist, a Shopify developer, a web developer, a designer, a content writer, a video editor, a project manager or account manager, and a reporting analyst.
Seniority and hours. Senior people cost more than junior ones, and a dedicated shift for a US team is planned separately from our standard day.
Team size. The number of people, and whether each works full time on your accounts. See agency outsourcing.
Your margin is what is left of the client price after the delivery cost and your own time. Work it out in this order.
Delivery cost. What MMC invoices your agency for the scope.
Your own time. Account management, client calls and reviewing reports, priced at your team's internal cost per hour.
Client price. What the client pays you each month or for the project.
Margin is the client price minus the delivery cost minus your own time. Margin percentage is the margin divided by the client price.

Worked example, in illustrative units, not MMC prices. Delivery cost 100, your own time 25, client price 175. The margin is 175 minus 100 minus 25, which is 50. The margin percentage is 50 divided by 175, about 29 percent.

Markup is not margin. Adding 50 percent to a cost of 100 gives a price of 150, but the margin on that price is 50 divided by 150, which is 33 percent, before your own time. Quote from the margin you need, not the markup you add.

We do not tell you what to charge. We help you understand the effort in each scope, so your price matches the work. If you would rather buy fixed packages at a wholesale rate, see the SEO reseller programme.

blocks.h: What is and is not included
paras: Included in a scope: the work it lists, quality checks before anything reaches you, and reporting in your format.

Not included unless written in: ad spend, which the client pays to the platform; paid tools and software licences, which are agreed per scope; and new work outside the scope, which is quoted before it starts.

stages.k: Match the model to the work
stages.breaks: Pricing outcome work by the hour.
stages.why: Slow, careful work earns less than fast, careless work, and clients ask why the clock is running.
stages.does: We help you choose a model that fits the work, using hour blocks only where the task really is hourly.

stages.k: Close the scope on fixed fees
stages.breaks: Selling a fixed fee with an open scope.
stages.why: The client keeps asking, the fee does not change, and your margin pays for the difference.
stages.does: Fixed projects have a written scope and change rules, so anything extra is quoted before work starts.

stages.breaks: Offering a retainer with no deliverable list.
stages.why: A client who does not know what they get each month assumes it is everything.
stages.does: We write the monthly deliverables and the review rhythm into the scope, so the retainer is easy to defend.

stages.breaks: Forgetting costs that sit outside the fee.
stages.why: Ad spend, licences and tools are real costs that someone has to carry.
stages.does: The agreement states who pays for ad spend and tools, so no cost is a surprise to you or your client.

stages.why: Too low and you carry the risk. Too high and a competitor wins the pitch.
stages.does: We explain delivery costs under the agreement, and you set a client price knowing your margin.
